facts.text: Founded in 1947 as a Lehrerleut Bruderhof by families led by preacher Johann Wipf from Alberta’s Miami Hutterite Colony, it remains an agricultural settlement of the Hutterian Brethren.
Migration into Montana in the late 1940s was part of a larger Hutterite expansion, driven by the need for communal growth amid land constraints in Alberta.
Early years presented challenges in adapting to Montana's semi‑arid climate and continental weather patterns, requiring adjustments in irrigation and crop selection for self‑sufficiency.
Spanning about 0.4 square miles, the colony contributes to Montana farming through grain production and livestock, reflecting typical Hutterite economic practices.
New Miami Colony sits at approximately 48°11′31″N 112°16′52″W, placing it in central Pondera County amid the Great Plains transition zone.
The colony sits roughly 50 miles east of the Rocky Mountains' foothills, with the Blackfeet Indian Reservation about 20 miles to the north.
